vectors.enisa_quote: Intentional deactivation of security safeguards such as firewalls, virus scans, log monitoring
vectors.reason: ENISA gives no actor; firewalls, virus scans and log monitoring are controls of the ground IT estate and the lifecycle assets are production and control-centre systems, so the actor is implied to work from inside the ground systems, and no outside origin is named.

rows.sparta_quote: Compromising the ground segment gives an adversary the most direct path to first execution against a spacecraft
rows.reason: Firewalls, virus scans and log monitoring live in the ground systems; an actor inside them is the one who deactivates them and who can then push value changes on board.

rows.sparta_quote: transmit legitimate-looking commands to the target spacecraft
rows.reason: The internal-value changes ENISA lists reach the spacecraft as commands and table loads sent from the compromised ground system.

rows.sparta_quote: device and control registers, parameter and limit tables
rows.reason: ENISA's list of modified internal tables and registers is the definition of this technique; no candidate source proposed it.

rows.sparta_quote: Threat actors may target the internal registers of the victim spacecraft
rows.reason: ENISA names 'registers' literally and SPARTA's child technique is titled Registers.

rows.sparta_quote: short-circuiting MAC checks, widening anti-replay windows
rows.reason: Switching off the on-board checks that validate authority is a safeguard deactivation; ENISA also lists modified algorithms.
ENISA lists modification of cryptographic standards, i.e. weakening or bypassing encryption.

rows.sparta_quote: allow on-orbit selection of algorithms, keys, profiles, or “crypto off/clear” states
rows.reason: The 'crypto off/clear' selector states are a modification of the cryptographic profile in force; kept next to EX-0006 because ENISA names both 'algorithms' and 'cryptographic standards'.

rows.sparta_quote: suppresses or alters fault detection, isolation, and recovery (FDIR)
rows.reason: Silencing FDIR is the inhibited system recovery ENISA names; SPARTA files it under Defense Evasion, which is why the role stays evasion.

rows.enisa_quote: modification of the internal values of the satellite lifecycle assets
rows.sparta_quote: deliberate alteration of authoritative, non-executable settings or structured artifacts
rows.reason: SPARTA's wording for altered internal settings matches ENISA's modified internal values, tables and registers.

rows.enisa_quote: algorithms, cryptographic standards and other software components
rows.sparta_quote: deliberate alteration of the implementation that controls spacecraft behavior
rows.reason: Modified algorithms and software components are an alteration of the implementation itself.
